claims.text: The GitHub Copilot coding agent is a cloud-based autonomous agent that accepts a GitHub Issue as input, works independently in a GitHub Actions-powered sandbox environment, and delivers a pull request for human review without developer interaction during execution.
The Copilot coding agent runs in a GitHub Actions runner for minutes or hours and opens a PR when done, making it asynchronous, unlike VS Code agent mode, which is synchronous and interactive.
The Copilot coding agent applies built-in security checks (CodeQL analysis, secret scanning, dependency review) and produces PRs that pass through the same review workflow as human-authored code.
Agent mode in VS Code is available on all Copilot plans including Free, while the Copilot coding agent requires Copilot Pro+, Business, or Enterprise subscriptions.
The Copilot coding agent runs within a temporary isolated dev environment that is spun up so the agent can explore the codebase, make changes, build the code, and run tests.
The Copilot coding agent is a member of the repo that can comment on issues, open PRs, do code reviews, and use Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools to work with databases or cloud services.
When the Copilot coding agent finishes, it assigns the PR to the user and requests them as a reviewer, including a screenshot where applicable.
Reviewers can leave comments on the agent's PR, and the agent picks up the feedback, updates the PR, and notifies the user when finished.
A full Copilot coding agent session counts as only one premium request.
In VS Code, the 'Copilot on My Behalf' query in the Pull Requests view lists the agent's work, 'View Session' shows every command and decision, and the user can terminate the agent.
PR preview services such as Azure Static Web Apps, Vercel, and Netlify let reviewers check the agent's work without checking out the branch locally.
GitHub Agent HQ is a centralized orchestration layer that lets teams deploy, monitor, and compare GitHub Copilot, Anthropic Claude, and OpenAI Codex agents from a single interface.
In Agent HQ, agent selection happens through the Assignees dropdown on any GitHub issue, and the agents' work is standardized under GitHub's existing issue and PR model.
Agent HQ is included with all GitHub Copilot plans, with no separate marketplace purchase required, and works on github.com, VS Code, and GitHub Mobile.
Agent HQ supports a workflow of assigning the same issue to several agents side by side and comparing their pull requests.
GitHub launched Agent HQ to unite Codex, Claude, and Jules, letting developers manage multiple AI agents side by side from Mission Control.
Mission Control task entry points are github.com/copilot/agents, the /task command in github.com/copilot chat, the Issues page, and GitHub Mobile.

Mission Control lets users steer a running session through the chat panel, where Copilot adapts as soon as its current tool call completes, or by commenting on specific lines in the Files Changed view.

Recommended Mission Control review flow: check session logs first, scan files changed for unexpected modifications, verify CI passes, request a Copilot self-review of edge cases, and batch similar PRs.
Custom agents defined in .github/agents/ can be assigned to Mission Control tasks to give consistent specialized behavior, such as a security-reviewer agent.
In March 2026, Enterprise AI Controls added session filters for admins by status (queued, in progress, completed, failed, idle, timed out, canceled), repository, and user.
Mission Control lets users assign tasks to Copilot across repos, pick a custom agent, watch real-time session logs, steer mid-run (pause, refine, or restart), and jump to the resulting pull requests.
Agents working in parallel on the same repo can create merge conflicts if they touch the same files, so work should be partitioned; dependent or exploratory tasks should stay sequential.
Signals that an agent needs intervention include repeated failing tests or fetches, unexpected files in the diff, scope creep, misread intent in the session log, and circular behavior.
With OpenAI Codex under a Copilot Pro+ subscription, Copilot handles all model calls and standard rate limits apply, and VS Code's Agent Sessions view manages local and cloud agents in one place.
